I wouldn’t use that as app store release notes. It describes a promotion, but says nothing about what changed in the app. Apple asks “What’s New” text to describe changes in the version, and its rules restrict calls to buy digital subscriptions on a website in many storefronts. [Apple’s metadata guidance](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/platform-version-information), [App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/uk/)

Use a specific description of the actual update for the release notes. If the discount is also part of this release, tell me the platform and eligible regions before adding the website callout.

No. “Live sports intel for every game” is **32 characters**, including spaces; Apple’s [App Store subtitle limit is 30](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/app-information).

“**Live sports intel, every game**” keeps the meaning and fits at **29 characters**.

Yes, **if it describes what your app currently offers**. The text is within Apple’s 170-character promotional text limit. Apple also requires App Store metadata to be accurate, so use “sharper” and “faster” only if the alerts and insights have actually improved. Make sure “playoff season is here” fits the sport and regions where the text will appear. [Apple’s promotional text guidance](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/product-page/); [App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/)

If you want to avoid the comparative claims, use: **“Playoff season is here. Stay on top of the action with timely alerts and game insights.”**

I’d remove “Coming soon to Android!” from the iOS release notes. It doesn’t describe what changed in this update.

**Paste-ready:** “We fixed bugs and improved performance.”

If you have a specific fix users will notice, naming it would make the note more useful.
